messages:
maria_cs: FYI — merchant reported a weird change after last night's rollout. Their invoice autocomplete now chops off line-item descriptions halfway through. They say it used to include the vendor note and full description. Attached sample below from the customer (redacted).

maria_cs: Customer says it started ~2026-03-16 22:10 UTC after we flipped v2 routing. They gave a single API request/response example and a batch of invoices where lines were truncated.

maria_cs: example request/response (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-text-2026-optimized", "input": "Invoice line: 1x Steel Rods — length 2m, coating: galvanised. Notes:", "max_tokens": 64 }
```
```
response: "1x Steel Rods — length 2m, coating: galvan"  <-- customer expects "galvanised; handle with care"
request_id: req_01FZQJ9KXYZ
```

ben_support: ack. can you attach the customer's prompt logs + request metadata (route, model, streaming yes/no, sdk version)? we need the request_id and their org id.

maria_cs: pasted request_id above. org id is org_0042. They said they used non-streaming, python sdk v0.9.3.

alex_ml: curious if this is tokenization or a truncation SLO. can we get the full token-level output? ask for raw generation (no post-processing) and the token lengths. also which kernel/quant profile was used for redwood-text-2026-optimized — rollout might have swapped to quantized variant.

jordan_eng: tagging infra — @deploy-bot did we push a routing change or model-variant swap during the 21:45 deploy window? any canary logs? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deploy window 2026-03-16 21:30-22:00 UTC: rolled out routing config v2.7. No model binary swaps during that window. Canary metrics showed slight increase in tail latency (+8%) for small requests.

ben_support: maria, please ask the customer for a minimal repro — smallest prompt that reproduces the truncation, ideally with a deterministic seed or request_id. If streaming vs non-streaming differs, ask them to try streaming.

maria_cs: asked customer for minimal repro and full prompt logs. they provided an extra example with different phrasing — still truncated. forwarded.

qa_bot: collected logs for req_01FZQJ9KXYZ and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/customer-logs/org_0042/2141590000/req_01FZQJ9KXYZ.log

alex_ml: thanks @qa_bot. I'll pull the token-level output and check whether the decode/cleanup step truncated on a semicolon or non-ascii char. also check if prefix caching evicted mid-generation (prefix cache bug would explain consistent mid-line cuts).

jordan_eng: also want the route config for org_0042. can support run: 
```
redwoodctl routes get --org org_0042 --json > org_0042_routes.json
```
and attach here. looking for any policy that forces max_response_bytes or post-processing hooks.

ben_support: temp mitigation: ask customer to set `max_tokens` + 20 and see if it still truncates. if that fixes it, likely a mis-estimated token budget. If not, request full request logs (we need raw proto) and mark as high-priority.

maria_cs: sent mitigation steps to customer. they tried +20 and still saw cut at same char boundary.

alex_ml: I'm going to reproduce locally with the same model + request seed using the logs. if I can reproduce I'll open a regression in the model onboarding tracker with sample and token trace. if not reproducible we'll escalate to runtime team.

ben_support: creating a minimal repro checklist for the customer (so we don't get 50 invoice examples): 1) single-line prompt that triggers truncation, 2) exact `max_tokens`, `temperature`, streaming flag, 3) request-id if possible, 4) whether they post-process responses (truncate/strip), 5) sample complete invoice blob.

maria_cs: customer agreed to follow the checklist and will DM the minimal repro in ~30m. assigning to alex_ml + jordan_eng to triage once received. :pray:

jordan_eng: noted — will standby and watch S3 link. if alex reproduces, next step is to test with fallback model variant (non-quantized) to confirm whether quantization artifact is the cause.

alex_ml: added to my queue. will post updates here. if I find an obvious regression I'll include a small repro snippet we can use in CI to catch it.

ben_support: thanks team. setting priority P1 until we confirm if this is a runtime-level truncation vs customer post-processing.
